---
title: "API Conventions"
---

For lifecycle stages and the warning-to-removal process, see the project's [deprecation policy](https://github.com/jtrecenti/juscraper/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#política-de-deprecação).

## Standard Parameter Names

All scrapers in juscraper follow a unified API convention for parameter names.

### Search

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `pesquisa` | The search query string (canonical name) |

**Deprecated aliases:** `query`, `termo` — accepted with `DeprecationWarning`, will be removed in v1.0.

### Date Filters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `data_julgamento_inicio` | Start date for judgment filtering |
| `data_julgamento_fim` | End date for judgment filtering |
| `data_publicacao_inicio` | Start date for publication filtering |
| `data_publicacao_fim` | End date for publication filtering |

**Generic aliases:** `data_inicio` / `data_fim` map to `data_julgamento_inicio` / `data_julgamento_fim`.
Cannot be used together with the specific names — raises `ValueError`.

**Deprecated aliases:** `data_julgamento_de` / `data_julgamento_ate`, `data_publicacao_de` / `data_publicacao_ate` — accepted with `DeprecationWarning`.

#### Accepted input formats

Endpoints using the shared date-coercion pipeline accept the following formats for supported date filters. See `CONTRIBUTING.md` > **Schemas pydantic** > **Pipeline canônico (wiring)** for the implementation:

- `"DD/MM/AAAA"` — Brazilian short form (e.g. `"01/03/2024"`)
- `"DD-MM-AAAA"` — Brazilian with dashes (e.g. `"01-03-2024"`)
- `"AAAA-MM-DD"` — ISO-8601 short form (e.g. `"2024-03-01"`)
- `"AAAA/MM/DD"` — ISO-8601 with slashes (e.g. `"2024/03/01"`)
- `datetime.date`
- `datetime.datetime` (the time component is dropped)

The pipeline coerces every recognized input to whatever format the
tribunal's backend expects — eSAJ uses `DD/MM/AAAA`, REST/JSON backends
like TJDFT use `AAAA-MM-DD`. The exact backend format is declared per
schema via the `BACKEND_DATE_FORMAT: ClassVar[str]` attribute, so
callers don't need to know it. An empty string and `None` pass through
unchanged (open-ended search). An unrecognized format surfaces as a
single `ValueError("...Formato esperado: ...")` raised by
`validate_intervalo_datas`.

### Pagination

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `paginas` | `int \| list \| range \| None` | Pages to download (1-based) |

- `None` (default): downloads **all** available pages
- `int`: shorthand — `paginas=3` is equivalent to `range(1, 4)`
- `range`: e.g., `range(1, 4)` downloads pages 1, 2, 3
- `list`: e.g., `[1, 3, 5]` downloads specific pages

### Page Size

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `tamanho_pagina` | `int` | Results per page (default `10`; **TJES uses `20`** because of the Elasticsearch backend) |

`tamanho_pagina` is the canonical name across all tribunals that expose
page-size control. Each tribunal accepts exactly one deprecated alias —
the historical name from its specific backend — emitting
`DeprecationWarning`:

| Tribunal | Deprecated alias |
|----------|------------------|
| TJBA | `items_per_page` |
| TJDFT | `quantidade_por_pagina` |
| TJES (`cjsg` and `cjpg`) | `per_page` |
| TJGO | `qtde_itens_pagina` |
| TJMG | `linhas_por_pagina` |
| TJMT | `quantidade_por_pagina` |

Passing both the canonical name and the alias in the same call raises
`ValueError`. Cross-tribunal aliases (e.g. passing `linhas_por_pagina`
to the TJBA scraper) are rejected with `TypeError` via `extra="forbid"`.

## Parameter Support by Tribunal

| Parameter | TJSP (cjsg/cjpg) | TJDFT | TJPR | TJRS |
|-----------|-------------------|-------|------|------|
| `pesquisa` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `data_julgamento_inicio/fim` | Yes | Warned | Yes | Yes |
| `data_publicacao_inicio/fim` | No | Warned | Yes | Yes |
| `paginas` (all types) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `paginas=None` (all pages) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## Migration Guide

### From `query` / `termo` to `pesquisa`

```python
# Before
scraper.cjsg(query="direito civil")
scraper.cjsg_download(termo="direito civil")

# After
scraper.cjsg(pesquisa="direito civil")
scraper.cjsg_download(pesquisa="direito civil")
```

### From `_de/_ate` to `_inicio/_fim`

```python
# Before
scraper.cjsg(query="teste", data_julgamento_de="01/01/2023", data_julgamento_ate="31/12/2023")

# After
scraper.cjsg(pesquisa="teste", data_julgamento_inicio="01/01/2023", data_julgamento_fim="31/12/2023")
```

### From `data_inicio/fim` to `data_julgamento_inicio/fim` (TJSP)

```python
# Before
scraper.cjsg("teste", data_inicio="01/01/2023", data_fim="31/12/2023")

# After (canonical)
scraper.cjsg("teste", data_julgamento_inicio="01/01/2023", data_julgamento_fim="31/12/2023")

# Or (generic alias still works with DeprecationWarning)
scraper.cjsg("teste", data_inicio="01/01/2023", data_fim="31/12/2023")
```

### Pagination default change

```python
# Before: default was paginas=1 (only first page)
scraper.cjsg(pesquisa="teste")           # downloaded 1 page
scraper.cjsg(pesquisa="teste", paginas=3) # downloaded pages 1-3

# After: default is paginas=None (all pages)
scraper.cjsg(pesquisa="teste")            # downloads ALL pages
scraper.cjsg(pesquisa="teste", paginas=1) # downloads page 1 only
scraper.cjsg(pesquisa="teste", paginas=3) # downloads pages 1-3
```

### TRF3 `cpopg_parse`: from `htmls` to `brutos`

The TRF3 public portal stopped serving the JSF detail page, so `cpopg_download` now returns one dict of JSON API envelopes per CNJ instead of HTML. `cpopg_parse` takes those dicts as `brutos`; `htmls=` still works with a `DeprecationWarning`, but HTML saved from the old portal raises `TypeError` and must be downloaded again.

```python
# Before
htmls = trf3.cpopg_download(cnjs)
df = trf3.cpopg_parse(htmls=htmls, id_cnj_list=cnjs)

# After
brutos = trf3.cpopg_download(cnjs)
df = trf3.cpopg_parse(brutos, cnjs)
```

### TJAP `cjsg`: from `votacao="Unanime"` to `votacao="Unânime"`

The Tucujuris portal only recognizes `"Unânime"`, with the accent. On 15 Nov 2026, `votacao="Unanime"`, the spelling the docstring suggested up to 0.5.0, returned the same decisions as `"Maioria"`. It is now sent as `"Unânime"` with a `DeprecationWarning`, and will be removed in 0.7.0.

```python
# Before
tjap.cjsg("dano", votacao="Unanime")

# After
tjap.cjsg("dano", votacao="Unânime")
```

### TJGO `cjsg`: `id_instancia` takes the Projudi form values

The "Instância" dropdown of the Projudi search form offers `0` (all), `15` (Tribunal) and `151` (Turma de Uniformização / Turmas Recursais). The docstring suggested `1`, `2` and `3`, which the form never offered. `2` and `3` are now sent as `151` and `15` with a `DeprecationWarning`, and will be removed in 0.7.0. `1` (first degree) has no replacement, because the current form has no first-degree option: it is still sent as is, with a `DeprecationWarning`, until 0.7.0.

```python
# Before
tjgo.cjsg("dano moral", id_instancia=3)

# After
tjgo.cjsg("dano moral", id_instancia=15)
```

### TJSP `cpopg`/`cposg`: `method="api"` removed

The `api.tjsp.jus.br` lookup stopped returning processes (it answers `[]`
even for processes that exist), so `method="api"` was removed without a
deprecation cycle. Passing it raises `ValueError` before any request. Use
`method="html"`, the default; the HTML pages carry the same data and more.

```python
# Before
tjsp.cpopg("1000149-71.2024.8.26.0346", method="api")

# After
tjsp.cpopg("1000149-71.2024.8.26.0346")
```

`cpopg_parse` and `cposg_parse` no longer read the `.json` files the API
download used to save.

### TJSP `cjpg`/`cpopg`/`cposg`: failures stay in the result

A case or page that fails no longer drops out of the result with only a log
line. In `cpopg` (table `basicos`) and `cposg`, every requested CNJ has a row,
and the `motivo_falha` column is `None` for the cases read. A CNJ that was not
downloaded keeps a row with only the number and the reason: `nao_encontrado`
when the public lookup does not show it (no such case, or under seal),
`entrada_invalida`, `http_<status>`, `conexao`, `timeout` or
`resposta_inesperada`. Download and parse failures go into a single
`UserWarning`, and `cpopg_download`/`cposg_download` return them as
`{cnj: motivo_falha}`. The download also records them in
`falhas_download.json`, inside its `cpopg/` or `cposg/` folder, so
`cpopg_parse`/`cposg_parse` return the same failure rows as the one-step call.

```python
res = tjsp.cpopg(cnjs)
falhas = res["basicos"].query("motivo_falha.notna()")
```

A lost `cjpg` page has no row to carry the reason, so a partial read raises
`ColetaParcialError`, as in the eSAJ auto-chunk; the pages read are in
`.resultado`. Each page from the second on gets up to five requests, and an
HTTP error status counts as a failure; a page that fails all of them is lost
the same way:

```python
from juscraper.core.exceptions import ColetaParcialError

try:
    df = tjsp.cjpg("dano moral")
except ColetaParcialError as erro:
    df = erro.resultado
```

### Date format flexibility

Wired endpoints accept multiple input formats and coerce to the
backend's expected representation. The four examples below all produce
the same request:

```python
import datetime as dt
import juscraper as jus

tjsp = jus.scraper("tjsp")     # eSAJ backend (DD/MM/AAAA)
tjdft = jus.scraper("tjdft")   # REST JSON backend (AAAA-MM-DD)

# String, any of the four supported formats — coerced internally:
tjsp.cjsg("dano moral", paginas=1, data_julgamento_inicio="01/03/2024")
tjsp.cjsg("dano moral", paginas=1, data_julgamento_inicio="2024-03-01")
tjdft.cjsg("habeas",    paginas=1, data_julgamento_inicio="01/03/2024")
tjdft.cjsg("habeas",    paginas=1, data_julgamento_inicio="2024-03-01")

# Or pass a date / datetime directly:
tjsp.cjsg("dano moral", paginas=1, data_julgamento_inicio=dt.date(2024, 3, 1))
```

## Auto-chunking (eSAJ family)

Several eSAJ endpoints (`cjpg`/`cjsg` in TJSP and TJMS, plus `cjsg` in TJAC,
TJAL, TJAM, TJCE) cap each request at a one-year `data_julgamento_*`
window. When the user asks for a longer interval, the scraper
**automatically** splits the request into calendar-year windows, fetches
each one, and concatenates the results — deduplicating by `cd_acordao`
(cjsg) or `id_processo` (cjpg).

Each window ends the day before the same date one year later
(`01/01/2013`–`31/12/2013`, then `01/01/2014`–`31/12/2014`). The eSAJ
backend only accepts `data_julgamento_fim` strictly before
`data_julgamento_inicio` plus one calendar year and answers HTTP 404
otherwise, so a fixed day count would either drift or produce windows the
server rejects.

```python
import juscraper as jus

tjsp = jus.scraper("tjsp")

# Six-year span: scraper sends 6 requests under the hood and returns
# a single deduplicated DataFrame.
df = tjsp.cjsg(
    pesquisa="dano moral",
    data_julgamento_inicio="01/01/2018",
    data_julgamento_fim="31/12/2024",
)
```

The behaviour is controlled by `auto_chunk: bool = True` (default on).
With `auto_chunk=False`, a `data_julgamento_*` interval the server would
reject (end on or after the same date one year later) raises `ValueError`
before any request. This helps input validation paths that want to fail
before submitting a long job. `data_publicacao_*` is never split, so the
same check applies to it in either mode:

```python
tjsp.cjsg(
    pesquisa="dano moral",
    data_julgamento_inicio="01/01/2018",
    data_julgamento_fim="31/12/2024",
    auto_chunk=False,  # raises ValueError ("aceita no máximo 1 ano(s)")
)
```

If a window still fails after the HTTP retries (network errors, 4xx,
5xx), the scraper tries the remaining windows and then raises
`juscraper.core.exceptions.ColetaParcialError`. A partial result never
comes back as if it were complete. The error carries the work already done:
`.resultado` holds the deduplicated DataFrame of the windows that
succeeded, and `.falhas` lists `(inicio, fim, exception)` for the ones to
retry:

```python
from juscraper.core.exceptions import ColetaParcialError

try:
    df = tjsp.cjsg("dano moral", data_julgamento_inicio="01/01/2018", data_julgamento_fim="31/12/2024")
except ColetaParcialError as erro:
    df = erro.resultado
    print(erro.falhas)
```

TJMG `cjsg` and `cjsg_download` raise it too when a result page fails with another page already downloaded. The search stops at that page: `.resultado` holds the pages read before it (as a DataFrame, also in `cjsg_download`), `.falhas` holds only that failure, and the message lists the missing pages, to request again with `paginas=`.

DataJud's `listar_processos` follows the same rule. When a page fails (HTTP error, malformed response, a response with `_shards.failed > 0`, or a page that ends before the exact `hits.total`), the remaining aliases are still queried and `ColetaParcialError` is raised at the end. `.resultado` holds every record received, from all aliases, and each item in `.falhas` is `(None, None, exception)`; the error message names the alias and the page that failed.

Combining `auto_chunk=True` with `paginas` is rejected when
the interval is long enough to actually trigger chunking: the multi-window
semantics for `paginas` are ambiguous (each window? aggregated budget?)
and the design prefers to fail explicitly. For short intervals where
chunking is a no-op, `paginas` works as usual.

## Pre-scraping count (`count_only`)

Empirical legal research often benefits from a quick estimate of how many
results a query will return before committing to a long collection job
(~2 s/result in `cjsg`/`cjpg` with `sleep_time=0.5`, so 5 000 hits ≈ 3 h).
The `count_only: bool = False` flag — accepted by `cjsg` in TJAC, TJAL,
TJAM, TJCE, TJMS, TJSP and by `cjpg` in TJMS and TJSP — short-circuits the public
method to a single network call per window, extracts the total result
count from the first-page HTML, and returns an `int` instead of a
`pd.DataFrame`:

```python
import juscraper as jus

tjsp = jus.scraper("tjsp")

# One POST + one GET. Returns an int.
n = tjsp.cjpg(
    pesquisa="dano moral",
    data_julgamento_inicio="01/01/2024",
    data_julgamento_fim="31/12/2024",
    count_only=True,
)
print(f"Estimated wall-clock for full collection: {n * 2 / 3600:.1f}h")
```

Interaction with `auto_chunk`: when the interval exceeds one year and
`auto_chunk=True` (default), `count_only` iterates the disjoint windows
produced by `iter_date_windows` and **sums** the per-window counts. The
sum is raw — the de-duplication step that the normal path performs by
`cd_acordao` / `id_processo` does not apply here, so the returned number
can slightly overestimate `len(cjsg(...))` when documents are republished
across windows (same `cd_acordao` appearing in two windows). For most
estimation use cases this is the desired behaviour: the count reflects
what the backend will hand over, not the deduplicated final shape.

Other edge cases:

- `paginas` is ignored when `count_only=True` (the probe always inspects
  page 1). A `UserWarning` is emitted if both are passed.
- `auto_chunk=False` plus an interval longer than one year still raises
  `ValueError` — consistent with the strict path.
- Captcha or layout-change failures on page 1 propagate as `ValueError`
  with the same message as the regular path.
- Tribunals not yet wired reject `count_only` via `extra="forbid"`
  (`TypeError`).

The underlying helpers `cjsg_n_results(html)` and `cjpg_n_results(html)`
are exposed from `juscraper.courts._esaj.parse` and
`juscraper.courts.tjsp.cjpg_parse` for callers that already hold the
raw HTML.

## Full text of acórdãos (eSAJ)

`cjsg` returns the ementa and `cd_acordao`, not the full decision. In TJAC
and TJSP, `baixar_acordao(processo, data_julgamento)` downloads the PDF of
the acórdão and returns its path; `baixar_acordaos(df)` does the same for
each row of a `cjsg` DataFrame and adds `caminho_acordao` and
`motivo_falha`:

```python
import juscraper as jus

tjsp = jus.scraper("tjsp")
df = tjsp.cjsg("dano moral", paginas=1)
df = tjsp.baixar_acordaos(df)
df[["processo", "data_julgamento", "caminho_acordao", "motivo_falha"]]
```

The direct route of the `cjsg` (`cjsg/getArquivo.do`) asks for a login in
TJSP and for a reCAPTCHA in TJAC. These methods follow the process
movements in the second-degree consultation instead, as the R package
[`tjsp`](https://github.com/jjesusfilho/tjsp) by José de Jesus Filho does in
`tjsp_baixar_acordaos_cposg`: no login and no captcha.

- **Which acórdão.** A process may have more than one (the appeal and its
  embargos de declaração, often with their own `cdProcesso`). The method
  takes the first document whose type is an acórdão and whose movement date
  is on or after `data_julgamento`. The movement comes on the judgment day
  or a few days later, and the next acórdão of the same process comes after
  it. When two incidents have an acórdão on the same day, the date cannot
  tell them apart: the method returns the one from the incident listed first
  by the search, and a `logging` warning names the other.
- **What is returned.** The PDF as the court publishes it, at
  `<diretorio>/acordaos/<cnj>_<cdProcesso>_<cdDocumento>.pdf`. Text
  extraction is left to the caller. Long PDFs (100 pages and more in
  criminal chambers of TJSP) are a single acórdão with long votes, not a
  wider range of the case file.
- **Errors.** `ProcessoNaoEncontradoError` when the public consultation
  does not show the process: eSAJ answers the same way for a number that
  does not exist and for a process under judicial secrecy.
  `AcordaoNaoEncontradoError` when no acórdão is accessible from that date;
  the message counts the documents that asked for the process password.
  `RespostaNaoPdfError` when the PDF endpoint answers with something else
  (nothing is written). `RespostaInesperadaError` when a page is not in
  the known format. `EntradaInvalidaError`, a `ValueError`, when
  `processo` does not have 20 digits or `data_julgamento` is empty (`None`,
  `NaN`, `NaT`), in an unknown format or impossible (31/02); no request is
  made. In `baixar_acordaos` these become the `motivo_falha` values
  `nao_encontrado`, `sem_acordao`, `nao_pdf`, `resposta_inesperada` and
  `entrada_invalida`. All exceptions are imported from
  `juscraper.courts._esaj.acordao`.
- **Password-protected documents.** Documents that ask for the process
  password are skipped. If the acórdão of the requested date is one of
  them, the method returns the next acórdão of the process instead; a
  `logging` warning then says how many protected documents were skipped
  before the returned one.
- **Anti-bot block.** The first row that gets `bloqueio_anti_bot` ends the
  batch, because the block holds for the whole session: the following rows
  get the same reason without a request, and the rows already downloaded
  stay in the result. The same holds for TJCE and TJMS `baixar_acordaos` and
  for `baixar_sentencas`. Retry only the failed rows later or from another IP.
- **Pace.** `sleep_time` is the minimum interval between two requests to
  the court, also inside a single row: one TJSP acórdão takes the search,
  one page per incident, the movement pages and the folder of each
  candidate document.

### TJCE and TJMS: straight from `cd_acordao`

In TJCE and TJMS the direct route of the `cjsg` works without login or captcha, so
the methods take the codes of the `cjsg` row instead of the process number:
`baixar_acordao(cd_acordao, cd_foro)` makes one request to
`cjsg/getArquivo.do` and writes `<diretorio>/acordaos/<cd_acordao>.pdf`;
`baixar_acordaos(df)` reads the `cd_acordao` and `cd_foro` columns and adds
`caminho_acordao` and `motivo_falha`, as above:

```python
tjce = jus.scraper("tjce")
df = tjce.cjsg("dano moral", paginas=1)
df = tjce.baixar_acordaos(df)
df[["processo", "cd_acordao", "caminho_acordao", "motivo_falha"]]
```

`cd_acordao` already identifies one acórdão, so there is no choice by date.
When the court answers with an HTML page instead of the PDF ("Arquivo não
localizado" for an unknown code, or a captcha or login page),
`baixar_acordao` raises `DocumentoNaoPdfError`, from
`juscraper.courts._esaj.pasta`, and writes nothing; in `baixar_acordaos` the
row gets `nao_pdf`. A code that is empty or not only digits raises
`EntradaInvalidaError` (`entrada_invalida`) before any request.

TJAL and TJAM do not have these methods yet: the direct route asks for a
reCAPTCHA there, as in TJAC.

## Case documents of the first instance (TJSP)

Two methods download public documents of the first instance as PDF, with
no login and no captcha. Documents that ask for the process password are
left out (see jtrecenti/juscraper#481).

**Documents linked to movements.** `cpopg(..., download_pecas=True,
diretorio=...)` downloads, in the same session that lists the movements,
the PDF of each public document linked to a movement:

```python
import juscraper as jus

tjsp = jus.scraper("tjsp")
resultado = tjsp.cpopg("0000564-95.2025.8.26.0068", download_pecas=True, diretorio="pecas")
resultado["movimentacoes"][["data", "movimento", "cd_documento", "documento_publico", "caminho_documento"]]
```

- **Columns.** Every `cpopg` call (with or without `download_pecas`) now
  fills `cd_documento` and `documento_publico` in `movimentacoes`, read
  from the movement HTML with no extra request. `caminho_documento` has the
  PDF path, or `None` without `download_pecas`, for password-protected
  documents and for documents whose download failed.
- **Where files go.** `<diretorio>/cpopg/<cnj>/documentos/<cdDocumento>.pdf`.
  `cpopg` deletes its download folder at the end, so `diretorio` is
  required with `download_pecas=True`, is only accepted with it, and cannot
  be inside `download_path`. `cpopg_download(..., download_pecas=True)`
  writes the PDFs next to the process HTML.
- **Cost.** Two requests per public document (the folder page and the
  PDF), after the movement pages of the process: eSAJ only opens a document
  whose movement page the session has already loaded. The process page is
  not requested again.
- **Failures.** A document that fails (eSAJ refuses access, the answer is
  not a PDF, network error) does not stop the process: the HTML is saved,
  the PDF is missing, and a single `UserWarning` lists the failures at the
  end. A later `cpopg_download(..., download_pecas=True)` on the same
  folder downloads the process again only when a public PDF is missing, and
  requests only the missing PDFs.
- `download_pecas=True` requires `baixar_movimentacoes=True`; otherwise it
  raises `ValueError` before any request.

**Sentences from `cjpg`.** Each `cjpg` row has the four codes of the
"Visualizar Inteiro Teor" link: `cd_processo`, `cd_foro`, `nm_alias` (often
empty) and `cd_documento`. `baixar_sentenca(cd_processo, cd_foro,
cd_documento, nm_alias)` uses them to download the sentence PDF, and
`baixar_sentencas(df)` does the same for each row of a `cjpg` DataFrame,
adding `caminho_sentenca` and `motivo_falha`:

```python
df = tjsp.cjpg("atraso de voo", paginas=1)
df = tjsp.baixar_sentencas(df)
df[["cd_processo", "cd_documento", "caminho_sentenca", "motivo_falha"]]
```

The PDF goes to `<diretorio>/sentencas/<cd_processo>_<cd_documento>.pdf`.
Each sentence takes two requests (`cjpg/obterArquivo.do`, which redirects
to the folder, and the PDF), in any session, spaced by `sleep_time`. A code
outside the eSAJ format raises `EntradaInvalidaError` before any request;
in `baixar_sentencas` it becomes `motivo_falha="entrada_invalida"`. The
other values are `nao_pdf`, `resposta_inesperada` and the network reasons
of `juscraper.core.failures.MOTIVOS_FALHA`. The `cjpg` text column
`decisao` already has the sentence text; the PDF keeps the layout and the
signatures.

The routes are the ones of `tjsp_baixar_doc_movimentacao` and
`tjsp_baixar_sentenca_cjpg` in the R package
[`tjsp`](https://github.com/jjesusfilho/tjsp) by José de Jesus Filho. They
live in `juscraper.courts._esaj.pasta`. The movement route answers without
login in TJAC, TJAL, TJAM and TJCE as well, but those courts do not have
`cpopg` in juscraper yet.

TJMS has the same `cjpg`, with the same filters and columns, and the same
`baixar_sentenca` and `baixar_sentencas`. The 120-character limit of
`pesquisa` (`QueryTooLongError`) applies only to TJSP, where it was
measured. `listar_varas` and `grau="1"` in `listar_classes` and
`listar_assuntos` exist only in TJSP.

## Normalization Utilities

The `juscraper.utils.params` module provides normalization functions used internally by all scrapers:

- `normalize_paginas(paginas)` — normalizes `int | list | range | None`
- `normalize_pesquisa(pesquisa, **kwargs)` — handles deprecated aliases
- `normalize_datas(**kwargs)` — handles deprecated and generic date aliases
- `coerce_brazilian_date(value, backend_format)` — coerces any of the four supported string formats (or `date` / `datetime`) into the backend's expected format
- `apply_input_pipeline_search(schema_cls, method_name, *, ...)` — runs the canonical input pipeline (alias resolution → date coercion → interval validation → pydantic schema) for `cjsg`/`cjpg` endpoints
- `iter_date_windows(data_inicio, data_fim, *, max_dias=366, max_anos=None)` — splits a date range into non-overlapping windows for auto-chunking; `max_anos` switches to calendar-year windows
- `run_chunked_search(fetch_window, *, data_inicio, data_fim, dedup_key, ...)` — drives a search across windows, concatenates and deduplicates
- `warn_unsupported(param_name, tribunal)` — warns about unsupported parameters

## Rate limiting and retry behaviour

All HTTP scrapers that inherit from `juscraper.core.http.HTTPScraper`
share the same retry loop via `_request_with_retry`. Defaults:

| Setting | Default | Where to override |
|---------|---------|-------------------|
| Retried statuses | `403`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, `504` | constant `RETRYABLE_STATUSES` |
| Max attempts | `3` (including the first) | `max_retries=` per call |
| Backoff | `base_backoff ** attempt` → `2s` then `4s` (sleeps run between attempts 1→2 and 2→3; the 3rd failure raises `RetryExhaustedError` without sleeping, so the default `8s` from `2 ** 3` only kicks in with `max_retries >= 4`); each wait is capped at `max_backoff` (300 s) | `base_backoff=` per call; `max_backoff` in `politica=` (DataJud, JusBR, PDPJ, TRF3, TJMG, TJRS, TJSC) |
| Timeout and dropped connection | Not retried: the first `requests.Timeout` or `requests.ConnectionError` is raised | `retry_on_timeout` and `retry_on_connection_error` in `politica=`, for scrapers with HTTP profiles; already on in the profiles of TJMG, TJRS and TRF3 (both), JusBR and PDPJ (timeout only) and TJSC (connection only) |
| `Retry-After` (numeric seconds) | Honored when present | n/a |
| `Retry-After` (HTTP-date) | Ignored — falls back to backoff (#201) | n/a |
| Inter-request pause | `sleep_time=1.0` from the scraper constructor | `jus.scraper("tjsp", sleep_time=5.0)` |

The exponential backoff (`2s` then `4s` across the three default
attempts) resolves transient WAF blocks but does **not** always escape
longer cooldowns. If you see `RetryExhaustedError(status_code=403)`
(or `429`) repeatedly on the same scraper:

- **First**, increase `sleep_time` in the constructor so the pause
  between requests becomes longer than the WAF window. Doubling it
  (`sleep_time=2.0`) is usually enough for the TJSP eSAJ WAF.
- If that does not help and you are running from a corporate /
  institutional IP, the block is likely IP-based — switching to a
  residential network is the only reliable fix.
- The `403` retry is global; consumers that can reliably distinguish
  auth-failure `403` from WAF `403` (e.g. PDPJ, where `403` means
  expired JWT) keep a local retry loop in
  `aggregators/<name>/download.py` and opt out.
